title: Infinite-L: 'monotone hence Borel' false; uniform measure not identified

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: moderate (correctness of the infinite-$L$ construction).**

Definition "Averaged numerical meta-degree" assumes, for infinite $L$, a Borel product probability measure $\mu_1^{\otimes n}$ for which $a\mapsto s(\bar\varphi(a))$ is integrable, and justifies measurability by: *"$s$ is monotone hence Borel; $\bar\varphi$ is a composition of (assumed Borel) operations."* Two errors/gaps:

1. **"Monotone $\Rightarrow$ Borel" fails for partial orders.** It is true for a monotone function on a *linearly ordered* measurable space with the order topology. For a function merely order-preserving w.r.t. a **partial order** on a general measurable space it is false. For non-chain $L$ this justification is invalid; one must *assume* $s$ is $\mathcal B(L)$-measurable.

2. **No canonical "uniform/Lebesgue" $\mu_1$ for general infinite non-chain $L$.** The existence of $\mu_1$ is only exemplified by $L=[0,1]$. The problem explicitly asks *what structure on $L$ plays the role of the uniform measure*; for infinite non-chain $L$ this is left unanswered — the construction presupposes the very object to be identified.

**Required fix.** Either (i) make measurability of $s$ and existence of $\mu_1$ explicit standing hypotheses and present the infinite case as conditional; or (ii) replace the linear integral by a **Sugeno integral** $\tau(\varphi)=\sup_{t\in L} t\wedge\nu(\{a:\bar\varphi(a)\ge t\})$ against an $L$-valued capacity $\nu$, giving a measure-free, genuinely $L$-valued numerical degree (this is the construction the problem statement hints at).
